Lumen User Manual

How to import data, model it, write measures, and build interactive report pages in Lumen, a Windows desktop dashboard builder.

1. Getting started

Lumen works the way Power BI Desktop does. You bring tables in, relate them, define calculations, and arrange charts on pages. Clicking a chart or a slicer filters everything else on the page at once. It runs entirely on your own computer, and your reports are ordinary files.

What you need

  • 64-bit Windows with .NET Framework 4.7 or later. Current versions of Windows 10 and 11 include it.
  • To install Lumen, run LumenSetup.exe. It needs no administrator rights, checks for .NET, and puts Lumen on the Start menu. Windows may warn about an unrecognized app the first time, because the installer is not code signed: choose More info, then Run anyway. To remove it, use Settings > Apps > Installed apps; your reports stay where they are.
  • Enough memory for your data. In testing, 10 million sales rows used about 1.7 GB once loaded and peaked near 4 GB while loading.
  • For SQL Server import, a server you can reach with your Windows login.

Starting Lumen

Run Lumen.exe from its folder, src\Lumen.Desktop\bin\Release. Keep the DLL files beside it, since it needs them to start. To open a report directly, pass its path:

Lumen.exe "C:\Reports\Sales.lumen"

Your first five minutes

  1. On the Home tab, open Get data and choose Sample report. A three-page report loads, built on 50,000 generated sales rows.
  2. Click Bikes on the Sales by category column chart. The other visuals respond to that category. Click empty space in the chart to clear it.
  3. Tick North in the Region slicer. The cards and charts recalculate for that region. Untick it to go back.
  4. Click a chart, then click a different icon in the Visualizations pane. The chart changes type and keeps its fields.
  5. Press Ctrl+Z to undo that change.

3. Ideas to know first

TermMeaning
TableRows imported from one source. The source stays where it is, and Lumen keeps a copy inside the report.
ColumnA typed field: whole number, decimal, text, date, date and time, or true/false.
MeasureA named calculation written in LQL, Lumen's formula language. It has no fixed value. It is worked out for each bar, cell or card from the filters in force there.
RelationshipA link from a many-side column to a one-side column, such as Sales[ProductKey] to Product[ProductKey]. Filters flow from the one side to the many side.
Fact and dimensionA fact table holds the events (sales). Dimension tables describe them (product, date). Most reports filter dimensions and add up facts.
VisualA chart, table, card or slicer on a page.
WellA slot of a visual that takes fields, such as X-axis or Y-axis.
Implicit measureA numeric column dropped in a value well. Lumen summarizes it for you, usually with Sum.
BLANKNo value. Different from zero and from empty text.

4. Getting data

Open Home > Get data. After each import, Lumen looks for relationships to other tables on its own.

Text and CSV files

Choose Text/CSV and pick a .csv, .txt or .tsv file. Lumen works out the delimiter (comma, semicolon or tab) from the first line, and always treats that line as the column names. If your file has no header row, the first row of data becomes the names, so rename the columns with transform steps. If the real headers are on the second row, add a Use first row as headers step.

Excel workbooks

Choose Excel workbook and pick a .xlsx, .xls or .xlsb file. If the workbook has more than one sheet, Lumen asks which one to load. The table takes the sheet's name. To load several sheets, import the workbook once per sheet.

JSON files

The file should hold an array of objects, or an object with an array property. Lumen uses the first array it finds. Nested objects become columns with dotted names, such as address.city. Nested arrays are dropped.

SQL Server

  1. Choose SQL Server. The dialog starts with localhost.
  2. Type a server name, for example localhost or .\MSSQL2019. Half a second after you stop typing, Lumen asks that server for its databases and fills the Database list.
  3. Pick a database, or type its name if your login cannot list them. If listing fails, the message says why, and you can still type.
  4. In the bottom box, enter a table name such as dbo.Sales, or a query that begins with SELECT or WITH.
  5. Click OK.

Lumen connects with Windows Integrated Security, so it uses your Windows login and stores no password. A long-running query can take up to 5 minutes before it times out.

The server name, database and query are saved in the report file, and the query runs again on every Refresh. Only refresh reports from people you trust, the same way you would treat a script.

How column types are chosen

For each column, Lumen tries these in order and keeps the first that fits every value: whole number, decimal, true/false, date, text. Empty cells become BLANK. Change a wrong guess with a Change type step.

Refreshing

Home > Refresh re-reads every table and re-applies its steps. If a table fails, it keeps its old data and Lumen names it in a warning. Refresh cannot be undone. Tables from the sample are generated again rather than read from a file.

5. Shaping data

The Transform window cleans a table before it reaches your model. Each action adds a step to a list, and the steps are saved and replayed on every refresh. Your source is never changed.

Open it with Home > Transform, or right-click a table in the Fields pane and choose Transform data.

ButtonWhat it does
Use first row as headersTakes column names from the first row and removes that row.
Change typeConverts a column to another type.
Rename columnRenames a column.
Remove columnsDrops the columns you tick.
Filter rowsKeeps rows that meet a condition. IsBlank and IsNotBlank take no value.
Replace valuesReplaces one value with another in a column.
Split columnSplits text on a delimiter into Name.1, Name.2 and so on.
Add custom columnAdds a column from an LQL row expression, for example Sales[Qty] * 2. Use your table's name in the expression.
Remove duplicatesKeeps one of each identical row.
Unpivot columnsTurns the columns you tick into Attribute and Value rows.

Working with steps

  • A new step goes right after the selected one. Select the last step to add to the end.
  • Delete, Up and Down edit the list. Moving a step can break a later one that used a renamed or removed column. The status line then shows which step failed.
  • The preview shows the first 1,000 rows. The status line gives the full counts.
  • Close & apply runs all the steps on the whole table. Cancel discards this session's changes.

6. Data view

Click the grid button on the left rail. Pick a table on the left, and its rows appear in a scrolling grid. Scrolling stays fast with millions of rows, because rows are made only as they appear.

PropertyUse
ColumnThe display name.
Format stringHow values look. See format strings.
Summarize byThe default for an implicit measure: Sum, Average, Min, Max, Count, DistinctCount or None. Set key columns to None.
Sort by columnSorts this column by another. This is how Month sorts Jan, Feb, Mar and not alphabetically, using a hidden MonthNo column.
VisibilityHidden removes the column from the Fields pane. It can still be used in measures.
Mark asOn a date column, Date table marks it as the table's date key. Time-intelligence functions need this.

The grid is read-only. Change values in the source, or with transform steps.

7. Model view

Click the third button on the left rail. Each table is a card, and each relationship is a line.

  • Move a card by dragging its title.
  • Zoom with Ctrl and the mouse wheel.
  • Create a relationship by dragging a column onto the matching column of another table. The column with all-unique values becomes the one side. If neither is unique, Lumen refuses, because many-to-many is not supported.
  • Auto-detect relationships finds pairs with the same name and type, where one side is unique with no blanks.
  • Edit or delete by double-clicking a line. There you can set Active and Cardinality, or click Delete.

A second relationship between the same two tables starts inactive and shows as a dashed line. Inactive relationships carry no filters, and no function can switch one on for a single measure.

Filters flow one way, from the one side to the many side. A slicer on Sales[Region] will not narrow a visual that shows only Product columns with no measure from Sales.

8. Writing measures

Choose New measure on the ribbon, or right-click a table and choose it there. Double-click a measure in the Fields pane to edit it.

  1. Give it a Name. It can't repeat another measure, or a column in its home table.
  2. Set a Format string such as #,0 or 0.0%.
  3. Choose the Home table, which decides where it lists in the Fields pane.
  4. Write the expression. Typing [ after a table name lists its columns. A lone [ lists measures. ' lists tables, and a new word lists functions.
  5. Click OK. It stays open until the expression is valid.

LQL in brief

LQL is a subset of DAX. If you know DAX, most of what you write will work.

// Simple totals
Orders = COUNTROWS(Sales)
Revenue = SUMX(Sales, Sales[Qty] * Sales[UnitPrice])

// Measures can use measures. DIVIDE returns BLANK when dividing by zero.
Margin % = DIVIDE([Revenue] - [Cost], [Revenue])

// CALCULATE changes the filters for one calculation
Red Sales = CALCULATE([Revenue], Product[Color] = "Red")
Share of All Products = DIVIDE([Revenue], CALCULATE([Revenue], ALL(Product)))

// Time intelligence needs a marked date table
Sales YTD = TOTALYTD([Revenue], 'Date'[Date])
Sales LY  = CALCULATE([Revenue], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR('Date'[Date]))

// Variables keep long expressions readable
Tier =
VAR s = [Revenue]
RETURN SWITCH(TRUE(), s > 1000000, "High", s > 0, "Low", "None")

The name on the left of each example is what you type in the Name box. It isn't part of the expression.

Syntax rules

  • A column is Table[Column]. Quote table names that have spaces: 'Sales Data'[Qty].
  • A measure is [Measure Name].
  • Text uses double quotes.
  • Comments use // or /* */.
  • A bare column needs a row context. Sales[Qty] + 1 on its own is an error; put it inside an iterator like SUMX.
  • Operators, loosest first: ||, &&, comparisons and IN, & (join text), + -, * /, ^.

How a measure gets its filters

Each bar, cell or card asks for the measure under its own filters: its own category, plus slicers, the Filters pane and any selection. That is why one measure gives a different number in each place, and why a ratio's total is calculated fresh and not added up from the rows.

Where LQL differs from DAX

TopicIn Lumen
Measures inside iteratorsA measure or CALCULATE inside SUMX does not turn the current row into a filter. It sees the outer filters only, so it gives the same value for each row. Use columns inside iterators.
Division/ gives Infinity or NaN on zero. Use DIVIDE.
Minus and power-2^2 is 4 here. DAX gives -4. Add brackets.
CALCULATE predicatesA simple predicate must use exactly one column. Use FILTER for more than one.
INWorks with a literal list only: Product[Color] IN {"Red", "Blue"}.
FORMATUses .NET format strings.
VALUESSame as DISTINCT.
DATESYTD, SAMEPERIODLASTYEARReplace every filter on the date table, not only the date column.
Not availableUSERELATIONSHIP, ALLEXCEPT, RANKX, SUMMARIZE, calculated tables and calculated columns. Use an Add custom column step in place of a calculated column.

10. Building a report page

Add a visual

Use whichever is quickest:

  • With nothing selected, click a type in the Visualizations gallery or on the Insert tab. A new visual appears in the first free spot.
  • Drag a field from the Fields pane to empty page. A measure makes a card, and a column makes a table.
  • With nothing selected, double-click a field.

Add fields to a visual

  • Select the visual, then drag a field to a well.
  • Or select the visual and double-click a field. It goes into the first well that accepts it.
  • Remove a field with the × beside it.
  • A numeric column in a value well shows a list where you choose Sum, Average, Min, Max, Count or DistinctCount.

A visual shows a message until its required wells are filled.

Change a visual's type

Select one visual and click another type. Grouping fields move to grouping wells and values to value wells. Fields with no matching well are dropped; undo brings them back.

Select, move and resize

ToDo this
SelectClick the visual. Clicks on charts also select data, so you may see other visuals react. Press Esc to clear that.
Select severalCtrl+click, or drag a box from empty page.
MoveDrag the visual, or use the arrow keys. Shift+arrow moves 10 units. Slicers drag by their title.
ResizeDrag a handle on the frame. The smallest size is 48 units.
Skip snappingHold Alt while dragging. Otherwise visuals snap to an 8-unit grid.
Align by eyeDashed guides appear when an edge or center lines up with another visual.
Align exactlySelect two or more, then use View > Arrange. Space across and Space down even out the gaps.
StackRight-click, then Bring to front or Send to back.
CopyCtrl+C and Ctrl+V, or Ctrl+D to duplicate. Copies work inside one Lumen window.
DeleteDelete, or right-click and Remove.

Right-click menu of a visual

CommandEffect
Focus modeFills the page with this visual. Esc returns.
Show as tableOpens a window with the numbers behind the visual.
Export data (CSV)Saves those numbers to a file.
Copy as imagePuts a picture on the Windows clipboard.
Bring to front, Send to backChanges stacking.
RemoveDeletes the visual.

Pages

Click + beside the tabs to add a page. Right-click a tab to Rename, Duplicate or Delete it. Pages are 1280 by 720 units. Fit zooms to the window, and the slider sets any zoom from 30% to 200%.

The Selection pane

This lists the page's visuals, topmost first. Click a name to select the visual, which helps when one sits behind another. Hide takes a visual off the page. Lock keeps it from being dragged or resized with the mouse.

Undo

Almost every edit can be undone with Ctrl+Z and redone with Ctrl+Y. A full drag counts as one step. These are not undo steps: slicer choices, Refresh, and moving cards in Model view. Undoing a table import or a transform reverts the model, but the rows stay in memory until the report is reopened.

13. Filters

The Filters pane has up to three sections, each with its own scope.

SectionApplies to
On this visualOnly the selected visual
On this pageEvery visual on the page
On all pagesThe whole report

Drag a column to Add data fields here in the section you want. Then choose a filter type on the card.

TypeHow it works
BasicTick values from a list of up to 500. Nothing ticked means no filter.
AdvancedOne condition: equals, contains, starts with, greater than, is blank and so on. Click Apply filter.
TopNKeep the top or bottom N values of the column, ranked by a measure. Click Apply filter.
RelativeDateOn date columns: in the last N days, weeks, months or years. Click Apply filter.

Remove a filter with the × on its card. Filters can only target columns. To filter on a measure value, use TopN, or a measure with IF.

14. Slicers

A slicer is a filter that lives on the page. Add one, put a column in its Field well, and choose a Style under Format.

StyleUse
ListCheck boxes. Tick several to include several values.
DropdownThe same list inside a drop-down.
BetweenTwo sliders and two boxes for a number or date range. It filters when you release the mouse or leave the box.
RelativeDateLast N units on a date column. Click Apply or Clear.
  • Nothing ticked means All.
  • Slicers narrow one another when filters can flow between their columns. A slicer on Product[Category] narrows one on Product[Color], but a slicer on Sales[Region] does not, because filters don't flow from Sales to Product.
  • A slicer doesn't filter itself, so it keeps showing the choices you can still make.
  • A slicer applies to its own page. Lists show up to 1,000 values.
  • Choices are saved with the report.

15. Cross-filtering

Clicking a bar, slice or row selects it, and the other visuals respond.

  • Ctrl+click adds to the selection.
  • Clicking a selected mark clears it, as does clicking empty chart space or pressing Esc.
  • Only one visual on a page holds a selection at a time.

Choosing how visuals respond

ModeEffect on the other visual
FilterRecalculates for the selection only.
HighlightKeeps the full shape faint and draws the selected part solid.
NoneNo response.

By default slicers filter, and charts highlight where the target supports it. To change this, turn on View > Edit interactions, select the source visual, and choose a mode on each of the others.

16. Themes

View > Themes offers Light, Dark and High contrast. The theme is saved with the report. If Windows is in high contrast mode, Lumen uses its High contrast theme unless you imported a custom one.

Import theme reads a Power BI theme JSON file. Lumen uses name, dataColors, background, foreground, foregroundNeutralSecondary, backgroundLight and tableAccent, and ignores the rest.

17. Saving and recovery

Ctrl+S saves a .lumen file. It holds the pages, model, steps, slicer choices, theme and a copy of your data, so you can open it without the original sources. Sharing the file shares the data.

A .lumen file contains your imported rows, and the server names and queries used to load them. It contains no passwords.

Autosave and recovery

Every 2 minutes, if there are unsaved changes, Lumen writes a recovery copy to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Lumen\Recovery\autosave.lumen. A normal exit deletes it. If Lumen finds that file at startup, it offers to open it. Save a recovered report under a name of your choice.

CommandResult

Home > PDFAll pages, one per sheet. Pages are images, so text can't be selected. Lumen visits each page while it works.
Home > PrintThe current page, scaled to fit the sheet.

Copy as imageA visual on the clipboard. Right-click the visual.

19. Performance pane

The Performance tab shows how long each visual took after the last refresh, split into query and draw time. Use it to find the slow visual on a heavy page. Typical fixes are removing a high-cardinality column from a chart, replacing a slow iterator with a simple aggregate, or filtering a table down.

21. Troubleshooting

What you seeLikely cause and fix
Could not list databasesThe server name is wrong, the server is off, or your login has no access. Check the name, including any instance such as .\SQLEXPRESS. You can still type a database name.
A visual says a field no longer existsA table, column or measure it used was deleted or renamed by a transform. Remove the field and add another, or undo.
Visual totals look wrong across tablesThe relationship is missing or points the other way. Check Model view. Filters flow from the one side to the many side.
A blank row in a visualSome fact rows have keys with no match in the dimension. They group under BLANK so that totals stay right.
Year-to-date measures return nothing or look unfilteredMark the date column of your date table in Data view.
Months sort alphabeticallySet Sort by column on the month name in Data view.
Too many valuesThe query is over its row limit. Filter it or use Top N.
Measure gives the same number on each row of SUMXMeasures don't pick up the row inside iterators. See differences from DAX.
Infinity or NaN appearsA division by zero with /. Use DIVIDE.
Could not open the fileThe file is damaged, or was saved by a newer Lumen version.
A relative date filter looks a day behindA report left open past midnight can reuse a cached result. Click Refresh.

22. Known limits

  • No calculated columns or calculated tables in the model. Use an Add custom column step.
  • No many-to-many or bi-directional relationships. Inactive relationships have no effect.
  • Filters target columns only, not measures.
  • Advanced filters in the pane edit one condition.
  • Data is imported. There is no live connection to a source.
  • SQL Server uses Windows authentication only.
  • No publishing, sharing service, drill-through, bookmarks or custom tooltips.
  • Page size is fixed at 1280 by 720.
  • The ribbon stays light in Dark and High contrast themes.

23. Lumen Viewer

Lumen Viewer shows a finished report to people who should read it but not change it. It lives at src\Lumen.Viewer\bin\Release\LumenViewer.exe. Pass a .lumen file on the command line, press Open, or drop a file on the window.

To give it to someone, send them src\Lumen.Setup\bin\Release\LumenViewerSetup.exe. It is one file, and it needs no administrator rights. Their PC needs .NET Framework 4.7 or later; if it is missing, setup says so and Get .NET 4.7 opens Microsoft's download page. After installing .NET, run setup again. Setup puts Lumen Viewer on the Start menu, and offers to open .lumen files with it. If another app already owns .lumen files, that app stays the default and Lumen Viewer joins Open with. Windows may warn about an unrecognized app the first time, because the installer is not code signed: choose More info, then Run anyway. To remove it, use Settings > Apps > Installed apps.

The viewer never writes the report. Slicer and filter choices last until you close the window, and Reset filters puts them back as the file has them.

You canHow
Change pageThe list on the left, or Ctrl+Page Up and Ctrl+Page Down
FilterSlicers on the page, and the Filters pane for values of filters the author added
Cross-filterClick a mark, Ctrl+click for several. Click bare page or press Esc to clear
Look closerRight-click a visual: Focus mode, Show as table, Export data (CSV), Copy as image
Reload the dataRefresh data or F5 reloads each table from its source and applied steps. Press again to cancel. The new data is for this session; the file keeps what it had. If a source file has moved, the viewer looks for a file of that name beside the report
ExportExport PNG for this page, Export PDF for all pages, or Print (Ctrl+P)
Fit the screenFit, the zoom slider, or Full screen (F11, Esc to leave)
